title: accelerator-staging-sku-runway-playbook
body:
Purpose:
Short working playbook to align procurement cadence, staging lanes, and regional buffer rules for accelerator (H100/A100/L40) fleet through Q2 2026. This is a living doc — use as input to weekly procurement sync and SRE capacity review.

High-level goals:
- Maintain 12 weeks of burn runway for hosted clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 under base demand.
- Keep a 4-week emergency buffer for enterprise Dedicated pools in APAC (sg-sin-hk).
- Reduce per-token cost by 6–9% via SKU mix + leasing overlay through 2026 procurement windows.

Quick summary of assumptions (local notes):
- Vendor lead time ranges are noisy; treat quoted lead_time as median. Add 50% contingency for new vendor lanes.
- Swap/repair MTTR: 3 business days for on-site contracts; 10–14 days otherwise.
- Spot/lease fallback can cover up to 20% of short-term spikes but has higher per-hour cost and higher failure probability.

Current SKU snapshot (table, CSV-ish):
SKU, vendor, preferred_region, lead_time_days, procurement_mode, MOQ, current_inventory, committed_orders, expected_arrival, burn_rate_per_week, runway_weeks
H100-80GB, vendor-alpha, us-west-2, 42, buy, 8, 320, 64, 2026-04-18, 48, 6.7
A100-80GB, vendor-beta, eu-west-1, 28, buy, 16, 240, 128, 2026-03-22, 40, 6.0
L40S-48GB, vendor-gamma, ap-southeast-1, 35, lease, 4, 48, 0, NA, 12, 1.0
H200-prototype, vendor-alpha, us-east-1, 90, buy, 2, 6, 6, 2026-06-11, 4, 1.5

Interpretation notes:
- us-west-2 running slightly hot on H100s; committed orders will arrive mid-April and only bring runway to ~6.7 weeks at current burn. Need to either accelerate PO (expedite) or add lease coverage.
- eu-west-1 A100 replenishment looks OK but is dependent on regional customs clearance (we saw a 5–7 day slip last quarter).
- ap-southeast still heavily reliant on lease/partner pools — long-term plan to convert 20% of leased units to purchased over next two quarters if pricing holds.

Procurement pipeline states (quick checklist):
- PO draft -> finance approval -> vendor confirmation -> production hold -> shipment -> regional customs -> staging -> rack -> put-into-service
- Tickets: ensure each PO has a shipment SLA and an expedite clause flagged in the vendor_response field in JIRA INF-2124.

Lead-time heuristics and contingency lanes:
- Use median vendor lead_time_days + 14 days for customs/door-to-door.
- If lead_time_days > 60, route through secondary vendor lane (spot/lease overlay) and open broker queue.
- For orders with MOQ > 10, split into 2 tranches if region has limited staging capacity to avoid long inbound queues.

Scenario sketches (runway math quick):
- Base: demand unchanged. Compute runway = (current_inventory + committed_arrivals_weekly*weeks_until_arrival) / burn_rate_per_week.
- Surge x2 (temporary 3-week marketing event): require additional 96 H100s in us-west-2 to maintain 6-week runway. Options: expedite subset of committed orders (cost +12%), short-term leased pool (expected lead 2–7 days), or temporary traffic steering to eu-west-1.
- Region outage (eu-west-1 down 7 days): traffic reroute to us-west-2 increases burn by ~34% until autoscale cap reduced. Need 48 extra H100-equivalents in warm standby or aggressive throttling.

Capacity staging lanes (operational play):
- Crossdock staging (us-west-2): keep 2x staging bays at N. California colocation for receiving shipments. Purpose: speed customs -> rack.
- Regional buffer lanes: 4-week hot buffer in each major region, 8-week for primary hosted region.
- Broker/lease overlay: maintain relationships with 3 brokers, target negotiated hourly ceiling for emergency.

Risk log (short):
- Single-vendor concentration for H100s (vendor-alpha): medium risk. Mitigate: open A100/H100 alternates, increase vendor-beta allocation by 15% in next Q.
- Customs delays for EU imports: recurring. Mitigate: add 7-day buffer, allow split shipment.
- Lease price spike during GPU shortage: high impact on OPEX; mitigation: commit partial reserve with 3-month opt-out clause.

Action items (who / due):
- Maya: request expedite pricing for open POs with vendor-alpha and report cost delta by 2026-03-15.
- Diego: compile broker SLAs and sample agreements (3 vendors) and add to procurement runbook by 2026-03-22.
- Priya: validate customs SLA averages for eu-west-1 (last 6 months) and attach evidence to INF-2124 by 2026-03-18.
- Jonas: prototype traffic-steering rule that limits eu-west-1 CPU-heavy jobs under surge, PR to routing-policy repo by 2026-03-25.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Can we trial staggered MOQs with vendor-beta to reduce single arrival spikes? (ask procurement)
- Need a concise cost model that shows lease vs buy break-even at different shortage durations — aim for spreadsheet by next sync.
- Confirm whether Dedicated contracts require on-prem swap SLAs (impact MTTR assumptions).

Mini spreadsheet: 12-week forecast (week buckets, very rough):
Week, us-west-2 H100 available, eu-west-1 A100 available, ap-southeast L40S available, notes
W1, 320, 240, 48, baseline
W2, 296, 232, 44, committed shipments arrive (A100 partial)
W3, 248, 224, 40, marketing ramp begins?
W4, 200, 200, 36, lease overlay planned
W5, 160, 176, 32, expedite decision point
W6, 128, 160, 28, committed arrival (H100 tranche)
W7, 104, 144, 24, reroute test scheduled
W8, 88, 120, 20, reserve reorder trigger check
W9, 64, 96, 16, broker pool engaged if shortage
W10, 40, 80, 12, QC backlog risk
W11, 24, 56, 8, emergency procurement window
W12, 8, 40, 6, runway below 2 weeks for some pools

Meeting cadence and deliverables:
- Weekly procurement sync (Thu 10:00 PT) — short updates only: PO statuses, expedite requests, broker availability.
- Monthly capacity review (first Tue) — 1 pager snapshot to infra leadership.
- Emergency war-room: triggered if any primary region runway < 3 weeks.

Reference links / tickets (to attach):
- INF-2124 (procurement pipeline backlog), CONFLUENCE:INF-accelerator-runway-2025 (living analytics), SLACK:#infra-procurement (thread for expedites), GH PR: infra/procurement-heuristics (early heuristics).

Notes on document hygiene:
- This is intentionally informal — move finalized decisions into procurement-runbook/master when consensus reached.
- Keep sections short and dated when making material changes.

End of playbook snapshot.
